answer: Cross-epoch correlation lock: each identity's actions are scored against a behavioural vertex summarizing its prior-epoch transaction graph, and a new epoch's activity is only admitted if its distance to that vertex stays under a threshold. The rule anchors admission on continuity rather than registration, so a fresh identity must replicate the history the cluster expects or fall outside the tide of accepted activity. Fabricating that history costs an attacker one full epoch of consistent, non-rewarded transactions per identity, plus losing any prior gains if the profile shifts.
